findings.issue: The subject check is specified for ONE pair against ONE candidate, but the gate scans many candidates and a candidate can share many pairs. Two forks are undefined: (a) when a candidate shares 5 keys spanning 3 series — must ANY declared series pass, or ALL? (b) when a candidate's broad pair is subject-rejected, does the scan STOP (spec calls it «терминальный вердикт») or CONTINUE to the remaining candidates? Today _pair_rule_verdict (news_bot.py:2698-2734) deliberately keeps scanning after the first |B so a later |D can still win.
findings.why_matters: Fork (b) read as «stop the scan» silently disables the irreversible |D hard block whenever an unrelated broad pair is rejected first — that directly contradicts AC «поведение |D не изменилось» and removes the gate's strongest protection, and it also swallows a later legitimately-declared broad flag. Fork (a) read as ALL is strictly stricter than the rule the 3/3 and 1/21 corpus numbers were measured on, so the headline acceptance criterion would no longer hold on the very corpus that justifies the feature. Both are single-word implementation choices with opposite prod behaviour.
findings.fix: State in «Как должно работать» that: (1) a candidate passes if AT LEAST ONE shared pair has its series declared in both subject areas; (2) subject rejection removes THAT candidate from consideration and the scan continues over the remaining candidates (a later |D still hard-blocks, a later declared |B still flags); (3) terminality means only that after the full scan with zero surviving broad matches the gate returns «не дубль» without running set-overlap. Add an acceptance criterion for the multi-candidate case: rejected broad candidate + another candidate sharing a |D pair still yields [E015].

findings.issue: The load-bearing acceptance criterion («три известных настоящих дубля флагаются, из 21 ложного остаётся не больше одного») rests on a regression corpus that may not be constructible. Two of the three true dupes have no surviving fingerprint — the spec asserts they are «восстанавливаются прогоном extract_fingerprint», but that needs the ORIGINAL article body: published_articles drops paragraphs at move_to_published, and re-fetching autoevolution answers a bulk re-fetch with Cloudflare 403 (backfill_fingerprints.py:235-248 documents exactly this and refuses to persist). Titles alone cannot produce the shared pair key that is the precondition of the whole branch. The spec also never states that the corpus requires pulling the prod DB over SSH — there is no local DB in the repo.
findings.why_matters: If the two fingerprints cannot be reconstructed, the feature's single objective measurement collapses to 1 true dupe and the recall claim becomes unverifiable — the spec would ship a rule whose only evidence is an operator's title-level eyeballing. Discovering this during implementation blocks the whole feature at the last step, after the expensive test surgery is already done.
findings.fix: Add a data-availability line to «Тестирование»: name where corpus rows come from (prod SQLite pull over SSH), and state that the two dupes' fingerprints are recovered from the t-hunted side (fetchable) plus whatever autoevolution text is still reachable. Define the fallback acceptance criterion NOW: if a fingerprint cannot be reconstructed, that pair is asserted at title level only and the numeric criterion becomes «все восстановимые настоящие дубли флагаются (не менее одного), ложных ≤1 из 21».

findings.issue: Title as a proxy for «declared subject» is sound in the direction that matters (it does encode the operator's principle that a round-up mentioning X is not a dupe of an article about X), but the recall evidence is n=3, and all three happen to name the LINE in both titles. The systematic miss class is model-first headlines: autoevolution routinely titles by casting («This Ferrari F40 Is a Red Line Club Exclusive» is fine, «New Hot Wheels Ferrari F40 Costs $100» is not), where the line surfaces only in the body — and on the candidate side there is no first-paragraph fallback at all. Acronym matching is uppercase-only (RLC/STH/SDCC), so «novo lote rlc» silently fails to declare. Symmetrically, the surviving false class is unchanged in shape: line-named hubs («Last Car Culture Set for 2026», 56 pairs, 6 flags) still declare their line in the title and still flag against every single-casting post on that line — one such flag is the one false positive the measurement kept.
findings.why_matters: The overfitting mitigation (a suppression log) only detects misses if the miss class is named and the operator knows what to look for; «на всех шести проверенных постах t-hunted линия была в заголовке» is evidence about the source that is least at risk, not about autoevolution's model-first headlines. As hub/round-up titles increasingly carry line names, the false-positive class regrows without any signal that the rule degraded.
findings.fix: In «Риски», replace the six-post claim with the concrete miss class (model-first headline where the line lives only in the body; lowercase acronyms) and the concrete residual false class (line-named hub vs single-casting post on the same line). State that the suppression log must be readable enough to spot both, and set a review point («через месяц оператор пересматривает подавленные срабатывания») rather than leaving the mitigation passive.

findings.issue: The first-paragraph fallback is dead weight by the spec's own measurement: 0 new series across 6/6 sampled t-hunted posts (Risk 4), it cannot be exercised by the regression corpus, its only test would be synthetic, and it is unavailable on the candidate side by construction. Worse, it makes the rule order-dependent: article A declares the line only in ¶1, article B in its title — if A arrives second it flags, if A arrived first (and is now a candidate, title-only) the same pair does not flag. The corpus numbers 3/3 and 1/21 were measured on the TITLE-ONLY rule, i.e. on the configuration without this fallback.
findings.why_matters: It adds an unexercised branch inside a fail-open gate whose failures degrade quietly (one [E016] per hour), it can only ever ADD flags (the direction the feature exists to reduce), and it buys asymmetry that the spec then has to defend twice. Keeping it also means the shipped rule is not the rule that was measured.
findings.fix: Cut it: make the subject area the TITLE on both sides, which is exactly what the measurement validated, is symmetric, order-independent, and cheaper to implement and test. If the operator insists on keeping it (it was his answer in batch 2), record in «Ограничения» that (a) it is inert on all available data, (b) it can only add flags, (c) it makes the verdict depend on which article arrived second — and drop the sentence claiming t-hunted posts are «всегда на стороне новой статьи», which is false: every new article becomes a candidate for the next 30 days.

findings.issue: The mitigation for Risk 1 (overfitting — the feature's biggest risk) is a log line on a Docker host the operator reaches only over SSH, subject to container log rotation, and the spec asks only that it allow counting «сколько шума срезано». The project already has a purpose-built mechanism for exactly this: the intake funnel of per-tick counters rendered into the daily [E008]/[E009] admin ping (architecture.md:341, counters dropped_promo / dedup_block / dedup_degraded / held_for_review).
findings.why_matters: A count in a rotated log cannot answer the question the risk section says it will answer («не был ли проглочен настоящий дубль») — that needs both links, both titles and the shared line, reviewed by the operator, who in practice reads Telegram, not journalctl. Without a channel he actually reads, the mitigation is nominal and the overfitting risk is effectively unmitigated.
findings.fix: Add a funnel counter (e.g. dedup_suppressed) so the suppressed count rides the existing daily ping, and specify the log line's content — new link, candidate link, both titles, the shared line — so a swallowed dupe is identifiable after the fact. Optionally add a weekly digest line to the same ping listing suppressed pairs.

findings.issue: The acceptance criterion «Текст [E014] больше не содержит фразы "порог автоблокировки (50 %) не достигнут"» is unqualified, but that sentence is emitted unconditionally by the single E014 builder (admin_alerts.py:869-871), which also serves the set-overlap backstop path — where the sentence is literally TRUE (sim in [0.30,0.50)). The same over-broad wording applies to the log criterion: news_bot.py:4398/4438 index match['overlap_pct'] directly, so satisfying «лог больше не печатает процент» by dropping the key from the match dict raises KeyError inside the fail-open handler.
findings.why_matters: The spec promises twice that the set-overlap rule is untouched, then writes a criterion that degrades its ping text; and the sharpest failure mode of the log criterion is a silent [E016] degraded mode (capped at one ping/hour, so a systematic fault reads as a trickle) rather than a loud break.
findings.fix: Scope both criteria to the broad-pair path: «в пинге и логах broad-ветки не остаётся ни фразы про порог 50 %, ни процента пересечения; текст и лог backstop-ветки не меняются». Add a criterion that the change must not remove keys other code still reads — no new exception path in the gate.

findings.issue: No rollback lever is named. DEDUP_SERIES_ENABLED gates the entire pair rule, not the new subject check, so if the rule over-suppresses in prod the only recovery is a code revert and a manual redeploy — which the project forbids inside 10:00-20:00 МСК (rebooting resets the in-process day schedule). «Пользователь проверяет» says to watch for an [E015] spike but defines no action when one appears.
findings.why_matters: The spec itself rates overfitting as Risk 1 and expects a verdict only after 2-4 weeks of live traffic; a change whose correctness is decided in prod needs a cheaper undo than an out-of-window redeploy, and the operator needs to know in advance what he is supposed to do when the signal turns bad.
findings.fix: Either add an env kill-switch for the subject check alone (rule reverts to today's behaviour without a code change), or state explicitly in «Ограничения» that rollback = revert + manual deploy outside the publish window, and name the trigger («всплеск [E015]» / «пропущенный дубль в подавленных») that fires it.

findings.issue: The user-spec carries tech-spec-level detail: the test helper by name and line («_seed_published в tests/test_integration.py», «вызывается 26 раз»), a direct builder invocation in the verification table («python3 вызов alert_cross_source_dupe»), and the baseline test count. This is HOW/where, not WHAT/why.
findings.why_matters: It pins implementation choices before the tech-spec exists (e.g. that the fix lives at the gate layer and that the E014 text is verified by calling the builder directly), and it dates fast — line numbers and the 1970-test baseline drift with every commit on dev.
findings.fix: Keep the substance, drop the coordinates: «существующие интеграционные тесты сеют кандидату заголовок, не связанный с подставляемыми парами, — под новым правилом они перевернутся; правка этих тестов — самая объёмная часть работ». Move the helper name, call count and the builder invocation into the tech-spec / verification plan.

findings.issue: The terminality decision is framed as a binary — either fall into the set-overlap backstop (risking an irreversible [E015]) or skip it entirely. A third option exists at near-zero cost: after a subject rejection run the backstop in flag-only mode (a ≥0.50 verdict downgraded to [E014] instead of a block), or run it in shadow and only log what it would have said.
findings.why_matters: The chosen trade is directionally right — never convert a soft flag into an irreversible loss, and the backstop has fired zero times in 1.5 months — but it discards the 30-50 % net entirely for exactly the pairs that already look most similar, which is the inversion Risk 2 admits. Flag-only keeps that net with zero irreversibility, which dominates both options in the spec.
findings.fix: Name the flag-only / shadow variant in «Технические решения» and say why it was still rejected (e.g. «второй пинг по одной статье за тик недопустим»), or adopt it. If rejected, at minimum log the backstop's would-be verdict for subject-rejected pairs so Risk 2 stops being blind.

findings.issue: The rule makes two currently untested emergent properties load-bearing in prod: Portuguese title resolution (verified live but pinned by no test — the parametrised lexicon test is English-only) and extract_series() as a matching primitive, which today has no production caller at all. Neither is called out in the spec's edge cases or testing section, and the spec has no explicit edge-case list for empty/NULL candidate title or paragraphs=None (they exist in the interview, not in the document).
findings.why_matters: If PT matching regresses, the failure is silent suppression of every t-hunted flag — the exact source the feature is built around — and it degrades inside a fail-open gate that publishes on error. Degenerate title/paragraph values reach the new code on malformed historical rows.
findings.fix: Add to «Тестирование»: PT titles from the real corpus must be pinned by test, and the rule must treat a missing/empty title and paragraphs=None as «предмет не заявлен» without raising. Promote the edge cases already recorded in the interview into the spec.

findings.issue: M is defensible but sits at the top of the range and the spec understates two deliverables: building the prod-derived regression corpus (SSH pull, 31 pairs, fingerprint recovery, operator verdict labels) and amending the project knowledge that documents the current rule (architecture.md § dedup gate states «A shared |B (broad) key soft-flags» and «Both verdicts are terminal»; project.md repeats it). Neither appears in scope.
findings.why_matters: The corpus is the feature's only proof and its cost is data-extraction work, not code; leaving it implicit invites it to be squeezed at the end. Stale architecture docs on a gate described there as «bought with prod incidents and load-bearing» is how the next tuning decision goes wrong.
findings.fix: List the corpus fixture and the doc amendment as explicit deliverables. Consider building the corpus as a separately-landable first increment — it is independently valuable (it measures the CURRENT rule and gives the new rule a real baseline) and it de-risks the acceptance criterion before the test surgery begins.

summary: The diagnosis is measured, not assumed, and the core direction — require the shared line to be the declared subject of both articles, and keep the broad tier incapable of anything irreversible — is the right shape for this stack, with all data available at zero plumbing cost. Two things block approval: the check's behaviour across multiple shared pairs and multiple candidates is unspecified in a way that could silently disable the |D hard block or invalidate the corpus numbers, and the headline acceptance criterion depends on fingerprints that may be unrecoverable (bodies discarded at publish, autoevolution 403 on re-fetch).
